title: The spacetime Penrose inequality with charge and original-data rigidity

issues.description: The symbol c_* is used for two things. It is the coefficient in rho=c_* r^{-3-beta}, and it is also called the positive lower bound of rho on the fixed band b_3/4<=|h|<=b_3. These differ by a factor R_1^{-3-beta}. This is harmless because the band lies within a fixed radius, but it is a notational slip.
issues.evidence: sy:weights defines rho=c_* rho_0; the band step says 'the positive function rho has a fixed positive lower bound c_*'.

coverage:
Checked the numerical theorem end to end, by hand or symbolic algebra.
- End-preparation conformal identities: mu, J, field and I scaling, expansion. Energy-raising family E+2s via the flux 32*pi*s.
- Rest preparation: boosted Schwarzschild plane with |dy|^2-(v.dy)^2=|dx|^2, the bend lower metric bound, the Schwarzschild radial repair identity via the conformal Laplacian, and repaired mass m+2eA(inf).
- Filled scalar identity: the T block expansion, the positive-squares completion (the j^2 coefficient d(8+v)/(3q^2)), and the sharp gradient bound C(p,v)>=3/4, which is increasing in p.
- Mass cost: negative-part bound giving F_N>=-P_N(l+l^{1/2}). Conformal ADM coefficient -(1/4pi) times the flux of dt.
- Unmodified curvature bound from the system F=h and div V=u Xi together with the tau-absorption step.
- Flux projection: square completion I=|X|^2-|w x X|^2+|..|^2, two-form norm in gbar with d=1/D, and the scaling chain with lambda>=1.
- Second scalar solve: Y=B(y) reformulation, floor y>=y0, flux identity H0(0)/2*4piQ giving e_N=E(g_b)-H0(0)Q/2.
- Profile: L_opt discriminant equality 2 sqrt(1+2L'/L) e^y L=2e^y/s, integral 2s, L(0)=1.
- Neutral exterior: conformal scalar formula and discriminant step; pure-trace K'=-a gamma gives mu'=R/2+3a^2 and J'=2da; Young cost 5/2<3; arctan plateau condition uniform in M; trapped level-set boundary H-2a<0; full-cut comparison a'>=e^{2y0}a.
- Exclusion of e_N<=0 by energy raising. Optimisation s=Q/r_*, both branches. Passage j->infinity, and the reduction removing a non-timelike ADM vector.
- The cited neutral Theorem 1.3 (Sept-27 enclosing-area paper): its hypotheses (n=3, O_6/O_5 decay, q0 in (1/2,1), E>|P|, weakly trapped boundary, A_min>0) match how it is used. It is not circular.

Read but not re-derived:
- Height-gap barrier lemma and contact-exclusion lemma.
- Elliptic existence, a priori estimates and annular-replacement moment estimates.
- Rigidity sections (variation, stationary extension, Chrusciel-Wald maximal slice, Sudarsky-Wald staticity, Borghini-Cederbaum-Cogo uniqueness), only skimmed.
main_claim: One-ended 3D initial data with source-free E and B fields and charged dominant energy condition (DEC), weak decay (q>1/2), and boundary components each fixed-sign weakly trapped: then E>|P|, m>=Q, and r_A<=m+sqrt(m^2-Q^2), with r_A the minimum-enclosing-area radius. The polynomial bound m>=(r_A+Q^2/r_A)/2 is claimed only when r_A>Q. When m>Q and a connected, outermost, area-minimizing MOTS gives equality, the data are a slice of dyonic Reissner-Nordstrom. Proof idea: a coupled graph/conformal scalar system gives a charged scalar-curvature bound; a second flux solve turns charge into an energy drop sQ at area cost (1-s^2); then the neutral enclosing-area theorem is applied.
sibling_notes: Rests on the Sept-27 neutral enclosing-area paper (Theorem 1.3). Its prepared-comparison machinery (filled system, height bound b_1, polynomial bounds) is the same as here. Siblings rank136 and rank203 checked very similar charged-reduction chains (y-equation discriminant, floor test, pure-trace K, arctan ramp) and also reported no_gap_found; this paper agrees with them. The Riemannian charged-comparison proposition (cp:charged-comparison) is not used in the final numerical proof.
